author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected through a form reached by its address alone. The correction validates like booking and changes that visit in place.
acceptance_criteria: GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit form prefilled with that visit's current date and description
given a description and a date later than today, POST to the same address updates that visit in place, the pet gains no additional visit, and the response redirects to the owner detail page
given a blank description, POST refuses the correction, names the description, redisplays the form, and leaves the visit unchanged
given a date of today or earlier, POST refuses the correction, names the date, redisplays the form, and leaves the visit unchanged
the owner detail page offers no link to the correction form
edge case 3: a visit that does not exist or does not belong to the named pet is refused, on GET and POST, and no visit changes
edge case 4: a pet that does not belong to the named owner is refused, on GET and POST, and no visit changes
edge case 5: a visit whose date has passed opens prefilled, and resubmitting it is accepted only with a date later than today
edge case 6: a correction changes only that visit's date and description, and the visit stays on its pet
non_goals: Cancelling a booked visit (NG-5) or deleting a visit (NG-4)
Any edit link or other visible entry point to the correction form; the owner detail page is unchanged
Changing anything on a visit other than its date and description, including moving it to another pet
New or changed wording: no confirmation message and no correction-specific button label
Exempting a past-dated visit from the date-in-future rule
notes: Owner-stated contract from the intake request: reuse the existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit` model attribute. Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md per the owner's instruction to take the narrowest reading: a visible entry point; a description-only correction of a past visit; correction-specific wording and confirmation. Unknown visit, foreign-pet refusal, and edge case 6 extend the existing Visits refusal rule; the intake does not state them, so they are the narrowest reading of 'that visit'. Follow-up outside this expert's write scope: docs/adr/README.md index needs the new row for docs/adr/2026-10-30-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowing.md, and the system-design.md contracts and threat rows need the new route.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the owner aggregate and the VisitController seam (system-design § Contracts, invariants paragraph; § Scale and Load). No new type, module, or route family. The loader loadPetWithVisit takes an optional visitId, the PetController.findPet shape (grep basis; IDE oracle not connected). Without a visitId it books as today. With one it resolves the stored visit through owner and pet, and returns a detached copy as the `visit` model attribute, never adding to the pet. The POST handler mirrors booking: validate, refuse, else Owner.correctVisit(petId, visit), owners.save(owner), redirect to the owner. Template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm stays unchanged: a blank form action posts to the same address, the copy's id renders the non-new heading, the addVisit label stays, and no flash message is added. The date comparison moves to Visit so both routes share it (architecture-principles § Logic Placement); this is a TDD refactor step, not a refactor-first slice.
integration_points: Binding, GET and POST .../visits/{visitId}/edit: the target is a detached Visit copy (request-scoped, never a member of pet.visits), behind @InitBinder("visit") setAllowedFields("date","description"), in addition to the existing id disallow. Binding the stored visit is not the design: a refused POST would mutate the object the Previous Visits table renders.

Binding, Owner parameter: the correction handler must not bind the owner. Declare @ModelAttribute(binding = false) Owner owner, or otherwise read it without binding. Copying booking's plain @ModelAttribute Owner lets extra params such as address or pets[0].name reach the save and breaches edge case 6 (system-design § Known Defects, booking row).

Owner.correctVisit(Integer petId, Visit correction): the aggregate entry, shaped like addVisit. It finds the pet and the stored visit by the correction's id, and writes date and description only, through a Visit method. That method is the sole writer, which enforces edge case 6.

Pet resolves a visit by identity returning Optional (architecture-principles § Java Idioms). Absence throws IllegalArgumentException in the loader, the refusal booking's edge case 1 already uses, before any binding, on GET and POST. The message carries identifiers only (security-principles, secret disclosure row). Assert refusal the way the web harness surfaces a handler exception, plus no save.

Date check: Visit gains a method taking the day as an argument, false for a null date, with no ambient clock (architecture-principles principle 3 and § Logic Placement: a behavior method takes no dependency). The controller passes LocalDate.now(). Correction refuses on false with rejectValue("date","typeMismatch.visitDate"). Booking calls the same method and keeps its null guard, so its behavior is unchanged.

Double, OwnerRepository in VisitControllerTests: the existing @MockitoBean stub in a @WebMvcTest, a conscious exception: a hand-written double would implement the full JpaRepository surface. Assert outcomes on the returned owner graph; a save interaction is asserted only for the refused paths, where no outcome shows it.

Double, real persistence: one test in ClinicServiceTests (@DataJpaTest, real H2, no double) drives Owner.correctVisit then save and asserts the visit count is unchanged and the new values reload. The merge across the cascade is what a stub cannot show.
Double, HTTP transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned harness. Visit and Owner behavior gets unit tests with real objects in OwnerTests (testing-principles § Seams), no framework.

findings.description: The new correction POST takes a description with no upper bound, so input the column cannot hold is not refused at the boundary. Attacker path: any caller POSTs /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit with a future date and a description over 255 characters. `@NotBlank` (Visit.java:42) is the only constraint, and `grep -rn -E '@Size|@Length|@Max|@Pattern' src/main/java` hits only Owner.java:61 and Person.java:32,37. On PostgreSQL the column is `description TEXT` (postgres schema.sql:51), so an oversized value is stored and re-rendered on the owner and visit pages, bounded only by the container's form-size limit. author: system-design-expert
answer:
Placement: option (a). Add @Size(max = 255) on Visit.description, beside @NotBlank, in the entity layer. Hold the fix until the product question below is answered.

Layer. A length bound constrains domain state and holds at every entry point, so per architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog it is a business rule, not a request parameter's shape. The catalog's Form validator row reserves other homes for rules 'the type's own constraints cannot' express, and this one the type can express. docs/system-design.md Overview places form-level rules in bean-validation annotations on the entities. Person's name fields are the same form. Option (b) is refused: it is a fresh controller rule, and it contradicts the intake's 'validates like visit creation'. Option (c) is refused: a Visit method needs a controller branch per handler and repeats what the constraint already does. isDateAfter exists because the date check needs today's date, and that reason does not apply here.

Limit: 255, on all three vendors. It is the narrowest vendor column, so every vendor stores whatever passes. PostgreSQL's TEXT column has no limit to conflict with. The schemas stay unchanged, because the entity constraint is what makes the three vendors agree. @Size counts UTF-16 units, so a value that passes is never over 255 characters in a VARCHAR(255) column. No @Column(length) is needed: the schema is script-managed and the annotation would add nothing to it.

Wording: none added. @Size with no message uses the validator's default, as Person's names do. The bundles carry no Size key, so I18nPropertiesSyncTest and the prd-entry's no-new-wording non-goal are untouched. The description field already renders field errors through fragments/inputField.

Behavior on routes the slice's bullets do not name. The constraint changes booking (REQ-VIS-001), read from code and not run: on H2 and strict-mode MySQL an oversized description moves from an error page to a field-named refusal; on PostgreSQL an oversized description stored today becomes a refusal. The second is a real narrowing of accepted input. A PostgreSQL visit already stored over the limit still opens for correction, and its POST is refused until the description is shortened. That visit's other flows are not affected: no @Valid cascades from Owner or Pet to visits, and an unchanged visit is not re-validated at flush.

Product question: yes, booking's change needs a product-requirements-expert answer before the fix lands, per review-workflow reference § Processing Reviews step 2. This is the product expert's, not mine. Ask it for: whether the description bound is accepted on both booking and correction, whether that adds a PRD bullet or edge case, and the narrowing on PostgreSQL. Name line 16 and this response. My design input: the shared bound is the one form consistent with 'validates like visit creation'. If the product answer declines the booking change, do not fall back to (b): return to me, because a correction-only bound then contradicts the requirement and needs a design decision. If the product expert changes docs/prd.md, consult me again before the build-pass so the mirrored rows land.

docs/system-design.md:194 (now line 196) does not change. It says the entity constraints cover length, and the fix makes that true for this field. It is inaccurate only until the constraint lands. The Visit Contracts row and the Persistence section now record the bound.

Tests, once the product answer permits. One VisitControllerTests refusal on the correction POST: form redisplayed, description named, visit unchanged, no save. If booking is accepted, a matching booking refusal. Use the existing MockMvc and repository double of the sibling tests; no new double. No separate 255/256 boundary test is needed for a framework constraint unless the product answer makes the exact limit a stated requirement.

author: product-requirements-expert
answer:
Answer: no. A length bound on a visit's description is not accepted in this slice, on booking or on correction. This is a deferral for lack of an owner decision, not a decline of the bound on its merits.

Grounds. The intake's only validation statement is 'validates like visit creation (description required, date in the future)'. It names two rules, and neither is a length. The owner directed: 'take the narrowest reading consistent with this request and record the open question rather than waiting.' REQ-VIS-001's first bullet records a booking when a description and a later date are supplied, and it states no limit. A shared bound refuses input that booking stores today on PostgreSQL, so it revises REQ-VIS-001. No owner statement authorizes that revision, and the security reasoning is a rationale, not an owner decision. The narrowest reading is that a correction validates exactly as booking validates today, with the two named rules.

The three questions. (1) Bound on both flows, including the PostgreSQL narrowing: not accepted in this slice. (2) PRD bullet or edge case: none, on REQ-VIS-001 or REQ-VIS-003. (3) Exact limit as a stated requirement: no. The PRD states no limit. 255 is the design expert's proposed value for whoever takes the question up.

Correction-only bound: also out. It would make correction stricter than creation, which contradicts 'validates like visit creation'. Line 20 reaches the same conclusion.

Product outcome of the gap, read from code and not run. On H2 and strict-mode MySQL an oversized correction fails at the column and reaches the error page, and the visit does not change. REQ-SYS-002 already specifies that page and bars internal detail from it. On PostgreSQL an oversized correction is stored, as an oversized booking is today. Line 16 rates this LOW-MEDIUM and records no stored-visit corruption on H2 or strict-mode MySQL. The correction route adds a path to a gap booking already has, and it adds no new kind of outcome. Non-strict MySQL was not examined in line 16; that is for the design expert.

Recorded. docs/prd.md Open Questions gains 'Should a visit's description have a length limit?'. No Non-Goals row and no non-goal ADR: the owner has not declined the bound, so a row would claim a decision that does not exist. The question resolves through a later owner decision, which would then revise REQ-VIS-001 and REQ-VIS-003 together. A shared bound stays the likely form at that point, per line 20, and that later change is cheap: one constraint plus tests.

Next step. Per line 20, this answer returns the fix to system-design-expert; do not add @Size and do not add a correction-only check. That consultation also carries the docs/prd.md change, as the build-pass gate requires. It needs to settle three things. First, the disposition of line 16: this answer takes the bound out of the slice's product scope, but the review finding stays open until its owners dispose of it. Second, line 20's system-design.md edits, which record a Visit constraint that will not land: the Contracts row Visit, the § Persistence sentence, and the length claim at line 196. Third, any Known Defects row for the gap, which is that expert's file. If the design expert or security-reviewer holds that the finding cannot stand unfixed, that is a conflict with this reading and goes to the human as a recorded consultation-request; it does not land as a silent bound.

author: system-design-expert
answer:
Short answer: line 16 cannot be disposed of by me, by you, or by line 23. Only the human can decide it. Items (2) and (3) are done. Do not append a build-pass. Append a consultation-request with target human, using the question below. That is the conflict with line 23 that lines 23 and 24 both said goes to the human.

(1) Line 16. It does not stand as a recorded gap on agent authority. A blocked tag means a defect that must not merge unfixed (review-workflow § feedback tags). Three things bar a paper disposition. First, the finding has a basis in the brief: security-principles § Trust Boundaries requires range validation where external input arrives, for every boundary a change crosses, and § Applying this section says what a change introduces is always a finding. The new POST is such a boundary. The unbounded description is not among the baseline absences that section excuses, because system-design § Security Context does not list it. Second, that brief states the project decides how to meet the laws, never whether. Its § Standing Gaps is the one list a reviewer stands down on, it is outside my write scope, and an entry there is the owner's acceptance. Third, a design-doc line telling the reviewer not to raise this would be a document granting itself a reviewer-check exemption, itself a Critical blocked finding. Reviewers judge against the briefs, never against this response, so a Known Defects row does not stop a re-review from raising it, and it must not try to. The intake's 'take the narrowest reading and record the open question' properly supports line 23's product reading. It is not acceptance of a blocked security finding: the owner stated no such thing, and its 'no further product answer will come' does not make an agent the acceptor. If no reply can arrive, the recorded pause is the correct end of the run (CLAUDE.md § Pipeline Routing).

My design position, for the human to weigh: the shared bound on the entity, as placed in line 20, remains the right fix. A correction-only bound stays refused. I do not reopen line 23's product reading; the two positions conflict and neither of us can settle it.

Question to put to the human, in your words but with these facts: 'The new visit correction POST accepts a description of any length, as booking does. The security reviewer rated this LOW-MEDIUM and blocked merge. The product expert kept a limit out of this slice because you stated none. Decide one. (A) Add a 255-character limit to the visit description on both booking and correction. This revises REQ-VIS-001 and REQ-VIS-003, and on PostgreSQL it refuses long descriptions accepted today. A visit already stored over the limit cannot be corrected until shortened. (B) Accept the gap for now. Nothing changes in code, the gap is listed in security-principles § Standing Gaps, and the length-limit question stays open.' Recommend (A). State that the answer to (B) must come from the human, and that restating the request decides nothing.

On (A), consult product-requirements-expert for the PRD revision, then me to restore the rows, then land @Size and the tests per line 20. On (B), the accepted gap needs its Standing Gaps entry before the re-review, and that brief is not mine or yours to edit without that decision; ask root who carries the edit (CLAUDE.md § Confirmation Discipline, durable instructions). Line 16's fix round then has nothing to apply.

(2) Line 20's edits: corrected, and this replaces line 20's statement that line 196 stays unchanged. The Visit Contracts row no longer claims a bound. § Persistence now states the columns differ and no entity constraint bounds the description. The Threat Model row now limits the length claim to a person's names and names the visit description as unbounded. These describe the code as it stands and hold under either human answer until code changes.

(3) Known Defects row: added, derived and unconfirmed, with no requirement breached, because no requirement states a limit. It records the behavior and is no disposition of line 16.

Non-strict MySQL does not change the rating under the shipped configuration. Connector/J 9.7.0 defaults jdbcCompliantTruncation to true, and setupServerForTruncationChecks adds STRICT_TRANS_TABLES to the session sql_mode when the server lacks it (read from the jar's bytecode, not run). So a non-strict server refuses as strict mode does, on the default datasource address. Silent truncation needs an operator to set jdbcCompliantTruncation=false through MYSQL_URL on a non-strict server. That one case would store a cut description. docker-compose starts stock mysql:9.7, and the conf.d directory it mounts is absent from this repository.

New evidence for line 16, run locally on H2 with an oversized POST to /owners/6/pets/8/visits/2/edit: status 500, and the visit stayed unchanged on the owner page. This settles the point line 16 left unverified. Under bootRun, where devtools is active, the HTML error page shows the update statement and the column definition. The packaged jar shows neither. So the disclosure reaches readers only in the development run, the already-recorded error-page defect (REQ-SYS-002), and it does not raise the rating. The rating itself stays the security-reviewer's call. Also worth stating to the human: owner address, owner city, and pet name carry @NotBlank with no length constraint either, so the class is wider than this field, and option (A) does not close those.
